name: Aromatic fougere

lead: Aromatic fougere is a fragrance style built around fresh herbs and lavender, often with woody and mossy undertones, and traditionally marketed to men. People wear it to smell clean, classic and groomed.
No studies look at it as a category. It is a perfumery style rather than a single product, and scent is one part of overall presentation.

paras: It is worn as a cologne or eau de toilette, usually applied to skin after showering, and is often chosen as an everyday or office scent. Many people layer it with matching grooming products.
Fragranced products can cause skin irritation or allergic reactions in some people, and perfume ingredients are subject to labelling rules.

angle.text: People use the scent as a finishing touch to grooming. It contributes to how a person is perceived in close contact rather than how they look.

lead: Aromatic fougere is a style of fragrance whose character comes from fresh aromatic herbs and lavender, typically with a woody or mossy base. It is widely sold as a masculine scent and used as part of grooming.

In perfumery classification, schemes such as the fragrance wheel have grouped lavender and aromatic herbs under an "aromatic" category.[1] Fougere itself has been treated as a family in older versions of that scheme.[1]
No published clinical studies address the style.

paras: The fragrance wheel places lavender and aromatic herbs in an "aromatic" subfamily within the fresh group, while the fougere group was moved away from the centre of the wheel in its 2010 revision.[1]
